$schema-note: Host-neutral pack definition — the single source of truth for pack identity, the dependency graph, and how a pack presents itself in a host catalog. Host manifests (.claude-plugin/*, .agents/plugins/* and .codex-plugin/*) are generated from this file by `npm run build-manifests`; CI fails if they drift. `presentation` holds product metadata in host-neutral terms — each generator maps it into that host's own shape (Codex calls it `interface`). See docs/packs.md.

marketplace.name: reply-skills
marketplace.description: Reply.io outbound expertise for AI agents — vendor-neutral SDR knowledge, Reply execution, and durable long-running work.

packs.name: ai-sdr-core
packs.description: Vendor-neutral AI SDR expertise: the SDR business-operation contract, outbound strategy and playbooks, and the guardrails that keep automated outreach safe. Provider-independent — no Reply.io knowledge required.

presentation.shortDescription: Run real outbound with guardrails, not guesswork
presentation.longDescription: Teaches an agent what an SDR operation actually is: 325 named operations in 21 families — find and verify a person, build an audience, plan and launch a campaign, work the replies, honour an opt-out, read the numbers honestly. Each one says what it reaches, whether it can be undone and what approval it needs, so sending and channel limits and explicit approval gates apply before anything reaches a real person. Vendor-neutral: it needs no Reply.io account and no provider at all.
examplePrompts: Plan an outbound campaign to book ten meetings with fintech founders
What sending limits should I respect on a brand-new domain?
Review this campaign and tell me what to fix before I launch
Which of these steps would reach a real person, and what do you need me to approve?

packs.name: reply-adapter
packs.description: Executes the AI SDR Core operation contract against Reply.io: the reply CLI, API v3, the MCP server, authentication and scopes, and translation of Reply-specific errors. Replaceable — swap it for another provider's adapter without touching the core.

presentation.shortDescription: Operate Reply.io from your agent — CLI, API v3 and MCP
presentation.longDescription: Turns the vendor-neutral SDR operations into real Reply.io calls: which endpoint group serves which operation, the order composite work must run in, how to authenticate and scope an API key, and what Reply's errors actually mean. Requires a Reply.io account and the AI SDR Core pack.
examplePrompts: Show me how my Reply.io campaigns performed last week
Import this CSV as a new list and tell me about the duplicates
Pause the campaign that is bouncing

packs.name: agentic-runtime
packs.description: Durable multi-session work: goals, plans, work items, checkpoints, resumability, execution reports and user memory in a plain-markdown workspace. Optional — skip it if your orchestrator already provides durable work.

presentation.shortDescription: Outbound work that survives a restart
presentation.longDescription: Gives an agent a plain-markdown workspace for work that outlives one session: goals broken into plans and work items, checkpoints it can resume from, reports of what a run actually did, and durable notes about the user. Optional — skip it if your orchestrator already provides durable work.
examplePrompts: Turn this goal into a plan I can resume tomorrow
Where did we leave off on the Q3 outbound push?
Report on what this run actually changed
